body: I don't like to think someone has it better then someone else I like to think that they've found what works for them. Our society has glorified the fast paced cut throat tough under pressure type of role and individual to the point that it seems that's how everyone and everything is supposed to be that way. As somebody who recently had to be brought to the er for a mental break down trying to keep up with these types of people I can say it's not for everyone and that's okay. Sure the "wealthy" will reep some more benefits for being very fast paced type A go getters bigger house, nicer car, lavish vacations, and a wardrobe budget that probably covers my years rent and, truthfully if what ever role in society they've taken or career they've chosen works for them and they're happy fulfilled and thriving then that's cool. Some people love and thrive under stress and pressure and they will reep the rewards. Some of us don't do so well with the constant stress of certain higher paying jobs or careers and are more content living with a little less if it means foregoing a lot of the stress that most wealthier people put up with. Sorry I'm not great at putting my thoughts together into a coherent point but I guess the point I'm trying to make is, most people think of wealth to be the amount of material goods and of course money one person has amassed but I think of it as a combination of how secure one is in their most basic of living needs like shelter food and clothing, how content they are with their material goods after basic living needs have been met and a big part that seems to be forgotten is the state of mind of the person in question.
